passed_evidence: Design normal total return was 490.25948608 percent versus 346.32062389 percent for buy-and-hold, with drawdown lower by 9.46329191 percentage points and Calmar 7.23883812 versus 4.48662523.
Validation remained positive under normal and stress costs, had five position changes, and passed frozen holding, terminal-liquidation-cost and annual positive-return breadth gates.
Normal annual total return was positive in all six fair-reset years and drawdown was non-worse in five of six years; positive-year return contribution was not dominated by one year.
material_failure: Validation total return was 121.68332476 percent versus 464.75475156 percent for passive BTC, capturing only 26.182266 percent of upside.
Validation drawdown was 34.42548508 percent versus 32.28416349 percent for passive BTC, so the liquidity filter increased drawdown by 2.14132159 percentage points instead of reducing it.
Validation Calmar was 3.53468730 versus 14.39575015 for passive BTC and reached at least seventy-five percent of passive Calmar in only three of six annual folds.
Validation had only two completed episodes and one winner; that single winner contributed 100 percent of positive completed-episode PnL.
Annual upside capture reached fifty percent in only two of six years, showing that positive aggregate return did not provide broad risk-adjusted participation.
material_learning: U.S. M2 growth acceleration was a strong Design-era risk-on timing proxy and correctly avoided much of 2022, but it failed to transport into 2023-2024: it missed most upside, slightly worsened drawdown, and depended on one positive completed Validation episode. Positive PnL and broad positive-year counts are insufficient when matched-capital Calmar, upside participation and episode support collapse.
